_why: Present in the vendor catalogue until the 2026-07-30 refresh, then removed. The hardware still exists, so dropping it would take away support someone already has. Delete this entry if the vendor lists id 2872 again.
_evidence: Entry copied verbatim from the registry generated at commit ed7c686. Family gen2 as classified by the vendor's own loader map at that time.
name: ry5088_mod007sv3he_uk_8k_soc

_why: Reported in issue #4. Never appeared in any vendor catalogue, so an extraction alone will not add it.
_evidence: Read sweep from the owner's board. GET_KEYMATRIX 0x89 returns a decodable yc500 keymap (Esc, grave, Tab, CapsLock, LShift, LCtrl down column 0); the gen2 read 0x8A returns all 0xFF; the yc500 sleep read 0x92 answers with four u16 at bytes 1..9. identify 0x8F returns 1748. That fixes the family as yc500, whose write paths are already [HW] evidenced on an X86.
_unknown: keyLayout and profile count were not observable from a read sweep. keyLayout Unknown renders a slot grid; profiles is pinned to 1 so nothing writes to a profile the board may not have.
name: epomaker_cypher81

_why: Reported in issue #9. Not in any vendor catalogue, so an extraction alone will not add it.
_evidence: Read sweep from the owner's board (0.2.1 web build). identify 0x8F returns 0x079F = 1951. GET_KEYMATRIX 0x89 returns a decodable yc500 keymap (Esc, grave, Tab, CapsLock, LShift, LCtrl down column 0); the gen2 read 0x8A returns all 0xFF; the yc500 sleep read 0x92 answers with four u16 (120, 120, 1680, 1680) and auto-OS 0x97 answers 1. That fixes the family as yc500, whose write paths are [HW] evidenced on an X86. Edge light 0x88 answers under its own opcode with plausible values, so the board appears to have one.
_unknown: keyLayout was not observable from a read sweep; Unknown makes the Keys page match a picture against the board and ask the owner to confirm it. Profile count was not observable either, so it is pinned to 1. The edge light's own layout name is not observable either, and the feature flag tracks that layout rather than the opcode, so sideLight stays false: better no control than one that cannot be drawn.
name: royuan_sky100pro

_why: Chronos 68 (Syntech): the vendor points it at Common68_ZAP68, a 67-key picture with no Right Ctrl. This board has the key. Reported for the Chronos in issue #8.
_evidence: The Chronos owner's keymap (issue #8) matched Common68_DK68HE, the same picture plus Right Ctrl, 68 of 68 keys. These four boards' own factory keymaps in the vendor data are byte-identical to it, so one baked layout serves all four. Local68_Chronos68 carries that geometry with slots from that keymap.
_unknown: ZAP68 is left alone: of its 33 boards, 26 have no Right Ctrl and would gain a phantom key. Two others that do have it, K68 id 2301 and HG68 HE id 3316, place other keys differently, so they keep matching their own keymap instead.
